question.problem: The equation ${x}^{2}-10x+50=0$ can be written in the form $(x+p)^{2}=q.$ Find $p+q,$ and solve the equation.
question.worked_solution:
We first move the constant to the right-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-10x+50 & =0 \\ {x}^{2}-10x & =-50\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we complete the square on the left-hand side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}-10x & =-50 \\ {x}^{2}-2\cdot 5x+{5}^{2}-{5}^{2} & =-50 \\ (x-5)^{2}-25 & =-50 \\ (x-5)^{2} & =-25\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $p=-5,\,q=-25,$ and $p+q=-30.$

We now solve the equation using the square root method.

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-5)^{2} & =-25 \\ x-5 & =\pm \sqrt{-25} \\ x-5 & =\pm 5\,\text{i} \\ x & =5\pm 5\,\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation has two solutions, $x=5+5\,\text{i}$ and $x=5-5\,\text{i}.$
